newsitem.title: USA: Grand Forks, N.D., pleads for U.S. disaster funds.
newsitem.headline: Grand Forks, N.D., pleads for U.S. disaster funds.

text.p: A group of political and business leaders from Grand Forks, N.D., urged Congress Wednesday to immediately enact an emergency disaster aid bill that would include $15 million in farm loans, $50 million to pay for livestock losses and $70 million for clearing debris from farm fields.
The legislation has been stalled for weeks in both the House and Senate over the issue of whether it should go to the White House with extraneous provisions certain to attract a presidential veto.
Grand Forks Mayor Pat Owens, two city council members and several businessmen told reporters at a news conference held on Capitol Hill that the flood-ravaged area urgently needed help.

"We have farmers in our states who can't plant; ranchers who are unable to renew their herds, and local school districts which are borrowing money right now to pay costs that should have already been covered by funds in this bill," the group said in a statement.
At the news conference, Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle threatened to hold the Senate in an all-night session Wednesday unless Republican leaders permit quick passage of the bill.

Earlier this spring, more than 1.1 million acres of North Dakota farmland was underwater when heavy winter snowfall melted. Grand Forks businesses suffered hundreds of millions of dollars in damage from the flood.
